q-6141.name: Question 1
q-6141.worked_solution:
To subtract $-37$ from $40,$ we combine the two negative signs to make a single plus sign. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}40-(-37) & = \\ 40+37 & = \\ 77 & .\end{aligned}
$$

q-186143.name: Question 6
q-186143.worked_solution:
To subtract $-1.5$ from $8$, we combine the two negative signs to make a single plus sign. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}8-(-1.5)=8+1.5.\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate $8+1.5$, we start at $8$ and move $1$ place to the right. Then, we move another $0.5$ places to the right: 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14150464/assets/6c5594e76467d574192f48b23ef994e9d86afbff76f3fb75c34082445e938774.png)

Thus,

$$
8-(-1.5)=9.5.
$$

q-43176.name: Question 7
q-43176.worked_solution:
To subtract $-6.5$ from $-1.5$, we first combine the two negative signs to make a single plus sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}-1.5-(-6.5)=-1.5+6.5.\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate $-1.5+6.5$, we start at $-1.5$ and move $6$ places to the right. Then, we move another  $0.5$ places to the right.  

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14150464/assets/e327ed5a6489a26d775b83c759c1e8ea21b5584797ce08f1a6e4419c99149392.png)

Thus, 

$$
\begin{aligned}-1.5-(-6.5)=5 & .\end{aligned}
$$

q-43178.name: Question 8
q-43178.worked_solution:
To subtract $-\frac{3}{2}$ from $1$, we drop  the parentheses and combine the two negative signs to make a single plus sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}1-(-\frac{3}{2})=1+\frac{3}{2} & .\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we express the two numbers as fractions over a common denominator of $2$
 and combine the numerators. This gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}1+\frac{3}{2}=\frac{2}{2}+\frac{3}{2}=\frac{2+3}{2} & .\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we work out $2+3$ using our number line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14150464/assets/c83beb4c78b8690dc04d2cc95bb20e94e33eac19962edea1055089adb4213ad4.png)

So we get

$$
\frac{2+3}{2}=\frac{5}{2}.
$$

Correct
EXPLANATION

To subtract −32 from 1, we drop the parentheses and combine the two negative signs to make a single plus sign:

1−(−32)=1+32.

Now, we express the two numbers as fractions over a common denominator of 2 and combine the numerators. This gives

1+32=22+32=2+32.

Next, we work out 2+3 using our number line.

So we get

2+32=52.

q-186221.problem: Expressed as an improper fraction in its simplest form, $\frac{3}{10}-(-\frac{11}{10})=${{field-1}}.
q-186221.worked_solution:
To subtract $-\frac{11}{10}$ from $\frac{3}{10}$, we first combine the two negative signs to make a single plus sign. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{10}-(-\frac{11}{10})=\frac{3}{10}+\frac{11}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

We have a common denominator of $10$, so we combine the numerators:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{10}+\frac{11}{10}=\frac{14}{10}=\frac{7}{5} & .\end{aligned}
$$

Correct
EXPLANATION

To subtract −1110 from 310, we first combine the two negative signs to make a single plus sign. This gives 310−(−1110)=310+1110.

We have a common denominator of 10, so we combine the numerators: 310+1110=1410=75.
